full_judgment:
Muhammad Imman Ali J. These civil petitions for leave to appeal are directed against the judgment and order dated 24.01.2018 passed by the High Court Division in Writ Petition No.543 of 2018. 

 2. The facts of the case, in short, are that Rumana Foiz, mother of Riana Joynab (daughter) aged 8 years 11 months and Rohan Jashim (son) aged 7 years 5 months, filed Writ Petition No.543 of 2018 before the High Court Division invoking Articles 27, 31, 32 and 44 of the Constitution for custody of her children, who at the relevant time were residing with her former husband and father of the children, Mainul Islam Chowdhury. At the time of issuance of the Rule on 24.01.2018 the High Court Division passed an ad-interim order to the effect that writ respondent No.1 (father of the children) was to hand over the children to the writ petitioner forthwith and that the children would remain with the writ petitioner during weekdays, i.e. from Sunday till Thursday. The writ respondent No.1 was directed to take the children on Friday morning to his place of residence and to return them to the writ petitioner's residence on the following Saturday evening. In addition writ respondent No.1 was allowed visiting rights to the children at the writ-petitioner's house every alternate day, after school hours with prior intimation to the writ petitioner. The High Court Division also directed the parties to take appropriate steps for final settlement of the issue of custody before the Family Court, with utmost expedition. 

 3. Being aggrieved by the interim order of the High Court Division the writ respondent Mainul Islam Chowdhury filed Civil Petition No.646 of 2018 (arising out of Civil Miscellaneous Petition No.89 of 2018) and the writ petitioner filed Civil Petition No.571 of 2018 (arising out of Civil Miscellaneous Petition No.91 of 2018). 

 4. When the matter came up for hearing before this Division, we directed the children to be produced before us on a date fixed. After speaking with the two children and their parents individually in Chamber and upon allowing the mother to stay with the children for some time, this Court ordered that till the matter is resolved by the competent court of law as directed by the High Court Division, both the father and the mother shall have joint custody of the two children. The order of the high Court Division was modified to the extent that the children would stay with the father from every Sunday to Thursday and after school hours every Thursday at 5:00 p.m. the children would be handed over to the Probation Officer, Department of Social Services, Chattogram appointed by the Court for taking them to the mother's house where they would stay till Saturday evening and at 6:00 p.m. on Saturday the Probation Officer would take the children to the house of the father. That order was directed to continue till the final decision is given by the competent court of law "or till disposal of the writ petition by the High Court Division." 

 5. Rumana Foiz then filed an application before this Division under Order XXVII Rule 1 of the Supreme Court of Bangladesh (Appellate Division) Rules 1988 read with Article 108 of the Constitution and the Contempt of Court Act, 1926, the application was recorded as Contempt Petition No.05 of 2018. She alleged, inter alia, that Mainul Islam Chowdhury (father of the children) and Ms. Paruma Begum (Probation Officer appointed by order of this Court) were flouting and violating the order and direction dated 01.02.2018 passed by this Division in Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos.646 and 571 of 2018. She alleged, inter alia, that the father of the children and the engaged Probation Officer were not complying with the order of this Court and failed to take the children to house of their mother as directed. Consequently, we modified our earlier order and have since received several reports from the Probation Officer, the Deputy Director, Department of Social Services, Social Services Office, Chattogram and Ms Mahjareen Binta Gaffar, Clinical Psychologist, Regional Trauma Counselling Centre, Chattogram Medical College Hospital, who was also appointed by order of this Court to provide Counselling to the children and their parents. 

 6. Upon consideration of the reports mentioned above, Contempt Petition No.05 of 2018 has been dismissed by judgment and order of this Court dated 08.10.2018. 

 7. In the light of the subsequent developments and in view of Contempt Petition No. 05 of 2018, this Court revisited Civil Petition for Leave to Appeal Nos. 646 and 571 of 2018 and passed an order dated 09.07.2018 directing that the Probation Officer be replaced by the Deputy Director from the Department of Social Services, Chattogram. By order dated 14.08.2018 the direction of this Court dated 01.02.20 8 in respect of custody of the children was maintained and Md. Shohidul Islam, Deputy Director was given the responsibility to carry out the direction of this Court in respect of the children. In addition this Court directed the Department of Social Services, to appoint a Clinical Psychologist for the purpose of counselling the children and their father and mother. 

 8. We have in the meantime received reports dated 28.02.2018, 21.3.2018, 08.04.2018, 30.04.2018, 22.05.2018 and 27.05.2018 from Ms. Paruma Begum, Probation Officer, who was initially appointed by order of this Court and also subsequent reports dated 03.09.2018 and 22.09.2018 supplied by Md. Shahidul Islam, Deputy Director. We have also received an undated report from Mahjareen Binta Gaffar, Clinical Psychologist giving details of her assessment and impression regarding the two children consequent upon clinical inter-views and observations on 03.09.2018, 11.09.2018 and 19.09.2018. 

 11. The principles of international law which guide us in case of custody of children are found in the Convention on the Rights of the Child (CRC), which pro-vides that the best interests of the child shall be a primary consideration when dealing with all matters concerning any child. The concept is not new since a similar provision exists in the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890, which provides for any order to be made under that law if the Court is satisfied that it is for the welfare of the minor that an order should be made. Hence, all courts of law .are bound to keep in mind these salutary provisions of law when dealing with custody, access and other matters which impact the lives of children. 

 12. It goes without saying that the best interests of any child requires that she/he be cared for by her/his parents. This is their innate right at birth. Article 7 of the CRC also provides that a child has the right to know and be cared for by his or her parents. Naturally, when the parents are at loggerheads, it would be the duty of the courts to ensure that the best interests of the child are protected. 

 13. Article 12 of the CRC provides that the child should be permitted to express her/his views freely in matters affecting her/him. This concept is also not new since the Guardians and Wards Act, 1890 provides that if the minor is old enough to form an intelligent preference, the Court may consider that preference. It is with such provisions in mind that we invariably speak to the children concerned in order to find out their views and preferences. 

 14. With regard to enforceability of provisions of international instruments, we may refer to the decisions in Hossain Muhammad Ershad vs Bangladesh and others, 21 BLD (AD) 69, where it was held that Court should not ignore the international obligations, which a country undertakes by signing the instruments. His Lordship, B.B.Roy Chowdhury, J. said that beneficial provisions of the International instruments should be implemented as the obligation of a signatory State. 

 18. We note from the order of the High Court Division that the order was passed as a temporary measure until disposal of the matter of custody of the children by a competent court, namely the Family Court. We are in respectful agreement with the view of the High Court Division that it is entirely within the jurisdiction of the Family Court to decide the issue of the children's custody. Hence, we find no purpose in keeping alive the Rule which is pending before the High Court Division. 

 21. In the light of our observations and directions, the Rule pending in the High Court Division in Writ Petition No. 543 of 2018 is discharged. 

 22. The Family Court is hereby directed to dispose of Family Case No.26 of 2018 expeditiously. Be it noted that the observations made hereinabove shall not have any bearing upon the trial and decision of the family case, now pending before the Senior Assistant Judge, First Court and Family Court, Sadar, Chattogram.
